gaps.sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
gaps.explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

gaps.sentence: They put ___ the meeting until everyone could attend.
The hotel was full, so we couldn't check ___.
gaps.explanation: check in = register; check out = leave and pay.

gaps.sentence: They want to try ___ the new software before buying.
gaps.explanation: try out = test something to see if it works.

gaps.sentence: You go ahead; I'll catch ___ with you later.
gaps.explanation: catch up (with) = reach the same point/level as somebody.

gaps.sentence: The doctors pulled him ___ after a difficult night.
gaps.explanation: pull through = recover from a serious illness.

gaps.sentence: She cheered ___ when she heard the news.
gaps.explanation: cheer up = become happier (also transitive: cheer somebody up).
